purpose: Centralized API system to monitor, control, and analyze data from hundreds of IoT sensors across multiple factory locations.

out_of_scope: Real hardware ingestion (sensor data is simulated/seeded)
status: Milestone M3 (Day 7): web UI for auth, sensors, profile and admin implemented

traceability_notes.API-001: Satisfied by the whole spec in docs/api-spec.yaml: OpenAPI 3, /api/v1 versioning, 429 rate limiting.
traceability_notes.API-002: Implemented in src/frontend/js/api.js: bearer token handling, single-flight refresh on 401, retry with back-off (GET/PUT/DELETE on network errors and 502-504; any method on 429), normalized errors. Real-time sync arrives with the dashboard (polling).

conventions.pagination: page (>=1) and page_size (1-100, default 20); responses include total and pages
conventions.rate_limits: Per user (per IP when not logged in): 100 requests/min. Per IP: 10 requests/min on login, register and resend-verification. In-memory, per server process. Health endpoints are exempt. 429 responses include Retry-After.
conventions.auth: Bearer JWT, access token 15 min; refresh token 7 days (30 with remember_me)
conventions.concurrency: PUT/PATCH on sensors honours If-Unmodified-Since; 409 on conflict
conventions.headers: Every response carries X-Request-ID and X-API-Version; limited routes add X-RateLimit-Limit / X-RateLimit-Remaining
conventions.bulk: Bulk create is all-or-nothing (422 if any item is invalid); bulk delete is partial and reports errors per id

assumptions: Sensor data is simulated or seeded; real hardware ingestion is out of scope.
A new account is inactive until the email link is clicked; self-registration always creates role 'user'.
The first admin is created by a seed script (Day 3).
Report generation runs in a background task; scheduled reports are checked by an in-process scheduler.
Passwords are limited to 72 characters (bcrypt limit).
Day 3: REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION=false so accounts are usable immediately; Day 4 turns it on and adds /auth/verify-email.
Refresh tokens rotate on every use; reusing a revoked token revokes all of that user's sessions.
Email verification is on by default (REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION=true). Development uses the console email backend, Docker uses MailHog.
An admin cannot demote, deactivate or delete their own account (prevents lock-out).
Deactivating a user revokes all their refresh tokens; their access token stops working immediately because it is re-checked on every request.
A user asking for another user's sensor receives 404, not 403, so sensor ids cannot be discovered.
Single readings are not audit-logged (high volume); bulk ingestion is.
Text input is sanitized (HTML tags and control characters removed) before storage.
The web app is a static single-page app served by the API at /ui (no build step); it talks to /api/v1 on the same origin, so CORS is not needed.
Access and refresh tokens are kept in browser storage; a strict Content-Security-Policy and DOM building without innerHTML reduce XSS risk.
Verification emails link to the web app (/ui/#/verify?token=...), which calls GET /api/v1/auth/verify-email.
